scope: New actual table material added to case-a, both full bilingual cases and unchanged rubric, for unchanged whole current682 compare-structure-to-reactivity competence. This is a new independent judgment of the correction, not a claim old reviewers already saw the added formulas.

wholeGoalFit.completeDemandDe: Die lernende Person kann ausgewählte Zucker anhand ihres molekularen Baus vergleichen und daraus ihr chemisches Reaktionsverhalten begründen.
wholeGoalFit.completeDemandEn: The learner can compare selected sugars based on their molecular structure and use this to justify their chemical reactivity.
wholeGoalFit.nativePageRole: Current PNG is explicitly a simplified building-block model; it does not pretend to provide complete maltose/sucrose formulas. New case material independently supplies those. No new D/V judgment here.
wholeGoalFit.caseA: Requires structural comparison and predicted qualitative reducing behaviour with explanation, rather than recalling the number of monomer units. The full table now makes the required structural evidence available.
wholeGoalFit.caseB: Retained fructose positive alkaline-test counterexample requires transfer to reaction conditions and accessible carbonyl forms, rather than a ketone-always-negative rule. A new full fructose formula is not promised in this task; the known ketose and positive observation form the puzzle.
wholeGoalFit.rubric: Both structural inference and conditional transfer are required; correct labels alone insufficient, and inference limits are assessed. No real laboratory execution or learner mastery is claimed.

maltoseStructuralScience.reconstructedIdentity: Two D-glucopyranose units, alpha glycosidic C1(A)-O-C4(B); shown alpha anomer at the free B-C1.
maltoseStructuralScience.glucoseHaworthConfiguration: For the stated O5/C1/C2/C3/C4/C5 orientation, OH at C2 down,C3 up,C4 down and C6 up describes D-glucose. A-C1 Og down is alpha. B-C4 Og replaces OH with the same stereochemical position; B-C1 OH remains free.
maltoseStructuralScience.completeness: All twelve carbons, both ring oxygens, one shared glycosidic oxygen, eight separate O-H groups and carbon-bound hydrogens are specified. There is no carbonyl left drawn in the cyclic representation.
maltoseStructuralScience.freeAnomericSite: B-C1 has ring-O and OH, hence a hemiacetal able to equilibrate with a reducing open-chain aldehyde form. A-C1 is glycosidically locked; a single free end still suffices.
maltoseStructuralScience.reducingInference: Under the stated comparable warm alkaline copper(II) assay without prior acid hydrolysis, maltose is reducing; the assertion is explained by the accessible free end, not merely two sugar units.

sucroseStructuralScience.reconstructedIdentity: D-glucopyranose alpha C1 connected through exactly one O to beta D-fructofuranose C2; both anomeric positions participate.
sucroseStructuralScience.glucoseUnit: G repeats the D-glucose OH pattern and C6-up convention, with G-C1 Og down (alpha).
sucroseStructuralScience.fructoseUnit: For O5 top,C2 right,C3 lower right,C4 lower left,C5 left, C3 OH up,C4 OH down,C6 up represent D-fructofuranose; C2 Og up is beta relative to C6, with C1-CH2OH down and no C2-H. Two CH2OH groups are explicit.
sucroseStructuralScience.anomericConsequence: G-C1 is an acetal and F-C2 a ketal; neither retains a free anomeric OH. The original glycosidic linkage does not expose an aldehyde/ketone by ordinary ring opening.
sucroseStructuralScience.reducingInference: Sucrose is not a reducing sugar in the stated comparison; prior acid hydrolysis has explicitly been excluded, so release of glucose/fructose cannot be invoked as though it already occurred.

representationJudgment.reason: Explicit cyclic connectivity, carbon numbering, each substituent including OH/H and above/below-plane positions uniquely specify the structures; a structural formula need not be a bitmap drawing. OH is an explicit oxygen-hydrogen group, not a missing heavy atom. Shared Og is counted once and has two bonds, no H.
representationJudgment.learnerDeliveryCaveat: The complete table block must actually be delivered with case-a, with OH/H and up/down not dropped by rendering. Merely naming the formula or linking this evidence root is insufficient learner material.
